newsitem.title: UK: Willis profits hit by currency, competition.
newsitem.headline: Willis profits hit by currency, competition.

text.p: International insurance broker and risk management consultant Willis Corroon Group Plc on Wednesday reported a five percent fall in profits as the strength of sterling and continued competition took its toll in the first three months of the year.

Profits before tax for the first quarter fell to 45.7 million pounds ($74.7 million) from 48.1 million pounds last year. After adjusting for the adverse impact of foreign exchange movements of 4.4 million pounds, underlying profits were up four percent.
Brokerage and fee revenue from continuing operations fell by seven percent to 184.2 million pounds.

Willis executive chairman John Reeve said the results were in line with expectations at the start of the year and reflected "intensifying competition" between underwriters which had led to further falls in premium rates.
